relations.subject: sgw:tls-server-connection
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - a default-secure-by-version behavioral fact; different in kind from requiresEdition (edition-gated feature) since this is a default that can be opted out of at any edition
relations.evidence: TLS is required by default for all communications with Couchbase Server [1]. TLS v1.3 is supported as the default protocol. [1] From release 3.0

relations.subject: sgw:bootstrap-use-tls-server
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - a config flag fully disabling a security requirement; not privilege- or role-shaped, so no promoted predicate fits
relations.evidence: Set this false in CLI or bootstrap file to turn-off off TLS completely — development and testing only

relations.subject: sgw:bootstrap-server-tls-skip-verify
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - a weaker opt-out than full disablement (encryption stays on, verification is skipped); distinct enough from disablesRequirement to warrant its own predicate
relations.evidence: Set this true in CLI or bootstrap file to skip server verification of certificates (self- or CA-signed) but leave encryption enabled.

relations.subject: sgw:tls-server-connection

cross_product_finding: This page's subject matter - TLS transport security between Sync Gateway<->Couchbase Server and Sync Gateway<->client (Couchbase Lite), configured via bootstrap/CLI flags and cert/key file paths - is a THIRD distinct authorization/security shape alongside this batch's channel/role sync-function model and the server RBAC model reused for Admin/Metrics API access. It is not privilege-shaped, not role-shaped, and not channel-shaped: it is boolean/path-valued configuration gating a default-secure transport behavior, closer in shape to server/'s edition gates (requiresEdition) than to any access-control relation, except the gate here is a config flag rather than a license edition. Also notable: this page again explicitly reuses Couchbase Server RBAC users (from the server/ batch) for Admin/Metrics API auth, reinforcing the users.md finding that Sync Gateway's security model is genuinely two-layered (own channel/role model for data sync + reused server RBAC for administration) plus this transport-security layer that sits underneath both and is orthogonal to either.
notable_absence: No audit-log-specific permission or setting appears on this page despite the coordinator's expectation that security/ pages might reveal one; TLS/cert configuration is the only 'security' concern covered here. Audit logging, if present in Sync Gateway docs, was not found on this page and may need coverage confirmation from another batch or a follow-up pass.
